text:
Maya P.: opened PR #7897 for the migration guide update. Heads-up: it includes a worked example that accidentally references a customer hostname and an internal IP. Need legal + security review before merging. preview: https://deploy-preview-7897--docs.redwood.ai :eyes:
Jonathan W.: thanks — can you paste the snippet here so we can triage quickly? CI preview looks green but linkcheck flagged the internal URL earlier.
Maya P.: copying the minimal excerpt below:
```yaml
example_integration:
  customer: "Acme Corp"
  api_host: "internal.acme.local"
  webhook_ip: "10.2.3.45"
```
Ashley N.: ok that definitely needs redaction. Suggest we replace with placeholders and an explicit note about obfuscated data. e.g. `customer: [REDACTED]`, `api_host: example.customer`, `webhook_ip: [REDACTED_IPV4]`.
Carol (Legal): quick guidance from legal: remove any real customer names or internal hostnames. Do not publish internal IPs or hostnames. Also add a short line in the docs metadata that the example data is synthetic. We'll need the PR to include a changelog entry referencing the redaction.
Maya P.: understood. Proposed replacement:
```yaml
example_integration:
  customer: "[REDACTED]"  # synthetic
  api_host: "example.customer"
  webhook_ip: "[REDACTED_IPV4]"
```
Jonathan W.: small ask from docs side — can we keep the example runnable (i.e., not break code fences) while redacting? maybe show `example.customer` for host and note to replace with your host.
Ashley N.: yep leaving it runnable is fine. Also running a grep across the branch to be safe: `git grep -n "Acme Corp" || true`. I'll push a tiny commit if anything else pops up.
security-bot: [scan] Sensitive-data-scan: 1 match found (internal IP) in `content/migration/examples.md` line 42. Recommendation: redact or substitute.
Maya P.: thanks security-bot. I pushed the redaction commit and updated the PR description with the legal signoff checklist.
ci-bot: build #7897-preview: success — docs preview generated at https://deploy-preview-7897--docs.redwood.ai/en/migration/examples.html
Carol (Legal): thanks — I reviewed the commit. Two final asks: (1) replace the exact path `/internal/portal` if present, (2) add `redacted: true` to the frontmatter for traceability. After that legal is fine.
Jonathan W.: frontmatter change is straightforward. Do we have a standard `redacted` frontmatter key? I can add it to the docs style guide note.
Carol (Legal): no mandatory key previously, but adding `redacted: true` plus a one-line `redaction_reason` field is helpful for audits. Keep the reason minimal (e.g., `contains customer PII`).
Maya P.: pushing a small commit now with frontmatter: `redacted: true` and `redaction_reason: "customer hostname/IP"`. Also updated the example as above.
ci-bot: build #7897-preview: success (2) — preview updated.
Ashley N.: did a quick grep — fixed one more occurrence in an ancillary example. All replaced with `example.customer` or `[REDACTED_IPV4]`.
Carol (Legal): approved from legal side once commits are in. Please ensure the PR description references the change and the audit ticket (AUDIT-423).
Maya P.: noted, added `AUDIT-423` to PR body and added a short changelog line.
Jonathan W.: I'm going to merge once we have a second docs review and security confirms there's no other sensitive content. @Ashley N. can you do a quick scan?
Ashley N.: on it, running `rg -n "10\.2\." content || true`. No other matches.
security-bot: [scan] Post-commit scan: no sensitive matches detected in branch `pr/7897`.
Jonathan W.: thanks everyone. I'll merge after CI finalizes in ~5m. If legal wants a snapshot of pre-redaction content for record, please let Maya know — we keep that in a locked audit bucket, not public.
Carol (Legal): yes, request that snapshot be stored securely (Maya follow-up ok). Otherwise legal approves the public doc. :white_check_mark:
Maya P.: will do. Thanks all — merging in a few mins after the final CI green. :rocket:
